messages:
anya: quick heads-up — saw weird deterministic token shift when serving the new quantized-4 model on long contexts (> 8k). seems like KV reads occasionally return values from ~+256 positions earlier, leads to subtle hallucination in long summaries.

anya: repro (minimal):
```
# run on dedicated dev pool, model: rwd-llamaq-13b-4bit
request: {\n  prompt: long_article (11200 tokens),\n  max_tokens: 1024,\n  use_kv_cache: true,\n}
```
logs snippet: `kv_lookup idx=8191 -> returned_frame=7935` (we see repeated pattern across traces).

anya: not sure if this is RoPE index scaling or a KV-window boundary bug after warmstart. tagging folks who touched RoPE adjustments last week. @carlos @ben

ben: pinged infra — which commit/tag are you on? any recent runtime flags?

anya: deploying `main@d8f9a2` (the quant commit). runtime flags: `--kv-window=8192 --enable-quant-fuse --rotary-scale=auto`

carlos: hmm `rotary-scale=auto` might pick a different scale depending on seq-len heuristics. if we warmstart with a small sequence then expand, the index->phase mapping can shift. do you have a trace across warmstart?

anya: yes. attached small trace (pasted):
```
[trace 00] seq=512 warmstart -> OK
[trace 01] expand to seq=4096 -> small drift
[trace 02] expand to seq=11200 -> +256 offset in a repeating pattern
```

carlos: that pattern sounds like a wrap/stride error in the KV store indexing, not purely RoPE math. could be an off-by-N when we shrink/expand ring buffer and recompute absolute indices.

ben: can you dump the raw kv-index map from the runtime? i.e., the mapping from request_pos -> kv_slot. a quick `curl` endpoint exists on the dev pool: `/internal/debug/kvmap?trace_id=...`

anya: i pulled one: `0..512 -> slots 0..512`, then `8192 -> slot 7936`. here's the line: `kv_slot(8192)=7936`. looks like `slot = (abs_pos % kv_window) - padding` maybe padding applied incorrectly when window changed.

eva: ran a local repro on my laptop with the exact binary and 4-bit quant. i can reproduce but only when `--enable-prefill-caches` is on. if i disable prefill, output matches reference.

eva: quick diff of tokens (token ids around the mismatch):
```
expected: ... 1203, 1209, 1216, 1223 ...
observed: ... 1203, 1209, 1192, 1200 ...  (shift by -24 tokens in that region)
```

frank: are users impacted? any alerting triggered?

anya: no prod alerts yet — only saw in canary with a couple of long-doc evals. suggests it's tied to long-context + quant + prefill path.

carlos: plan: 1) add an invariant check in runtime: after ring buffer resize, verify slot mapping by re-deriving indices from absolute positions. if mismatch, fail-safe to full cache rebuild. 2) add regression unit that simulates warmstart + expansion cycles on random sequences. 3) temporarily set `rotary-scale` to fixed (e.g., 1.0) for the canary.

ben: i'll add an alert rule to catch sudden repeated slot aliases (`kv_lookup` returning slot < abs_pos - 512 repeated > 3 times) so we can auto-detect in prod.

anya: adding a short reproducer script for CI (please review):
```
# repro_kv_warmstart.sh
# 1) start runtime with kv_window=8192 and rotary-scale=auto
# 2) send small prefill (seq 512)
# 3) send huge continuation (seq 11200)
# expect: no slot aliasing
python tools/send_sequence.py --model rwd-llamaq-13b-4bit --prefill 512 --cont 11200 --trace-id $RANDOM
```

carlos: looks good. small note — the runtime API for debug dump is protected in prod, make sure the CI can hit dev cluster only. i'll prepare a targeted patch to the ringbuffer resize code.

eva: i ran the repro across quant and fp16 builds. quant shows the aliasing, fp16 doesn't. so quantization interacts with prefill path (likely layout/packing differences).

ben: rolling a quick config change on the canary: `--enable-prefill-caches=false` while we patch. will monitor for regression in throughput/cost.

anya: thanks. i'll open a GH issue with traces and label `kvcache-bug` + `high-priority`. will also attach the CI repro.

frank: good catch — can we add an eval that compares final logits between fp16 and quant variants for long-doc prompts? would help catch regressions.

carlos: yes — we'll add a lightweight long-context invariant to Optimize evals: compare token-by-token divergence and flag > 0.1 KL shift after token 4096.

dev-bot: deploy request submitted by ben for canary config change (run id: dp-7738).

anya: action items: anya -> open issue + attach traces; carlos -> patch ringbuffer check; ben -> add alert & roll canary flag; eva -> run regression matrix (quant vs fp16) across long-doc suite. i'll follow up tomorrow with results. :white_check_mark:

ben: noted. will ping if canary shows anything unexpected. :mag_right:

carlos: i'll aim to have a PR by EOD. might add a fallback that rebuilds kv from scratch when invariant fails.

anya: thanks all — this felt subtle but surfaceable. will keep thread updated. :wave:
